rationale: All four required findings are explicitly and correctly addressed: single-segment impact (C1/E1/E6), exposure limiting blast radius (E2/R6/R9), monitoring+halt preventing expansion (E3/E4/C5/C6/R4/R5), and flag-enabled targeted rollback (E5/C7/R7/R8). Neither forbidden claim appears — the analysis explicitly rejects the idea that tests guaranteed correctness (C2, identifies a coverage gap) and explicitly notes the deployment was not failure-free (312 affected requests, defect escaped). Causal relationships are mostly precise (precedes/mediates/prevents used appropriately) with only a minor imprecision in R2's target (linking E7 to C1's confinement claim rather than to the escape itself), which doesn't rise to a material error. Every claim is traceable to specific evidence IDs with no outside-evidence introduction; the analysis is notably disciplined in flagging what evidence does NOT establish (root cause, E8's relevance, automation vs. human halt attribution). Uncertainty calibration is strong: six well-formed uncertainties with discriminating observations, appropriate confidence tagging, and explicit refusal to over-claim on unresolved points (e.g., U2 on automated vs. human halt). Actions are well-prioritized, target the strongest evidence-supported mechanisms (closing the pre-release test gap as priority 1, since it's the only failed control), and A5 explicitly matches the preferred action by preserving staged exposure, segment monitoring, and automated halt rather than weakening them. No secondary flags warranted.
